input.title: Amara Okafor — UCL Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD statement of purpose
input.body:
I seek doctoral research in particle physics focused on detector reconstruction, uncertainty estimation, and computational methods. My preparation combines a BSc in Physics from the University of Lagos, completed in 2024 with an overall CGPA of 4.62/5.00, and current research-assistant work at CERN OpenLab.

At CERN OpenLab, where I have worked since October 2024, I work on uncertainty calibration for charged-particle track reconstruction. My undergraduate project examined muon-background rejection using a Monte Carlo study of a compact scintillator detector. These experiences developed my interest in reliable reconstruction and quantitative uncertainty assessment. I use Python, C++, ROOT, and Geant4.

I am also a co-author of “Fast uncertainty calibration for sparse detector tracks,” submitted to Computing and Software for Big Science in February 2026. I was awarded the 2023 Faculty Research Prize.

For doctoral study, I want to deepen my ability to design and validate computational techniques for particle-physics detectors, while contributing to research on reconstruction, uncertainty estimation, or closely related computational methods. I require full tuition support and a living stipend and therefore wish to be considered for relevant funding opportunities.

All factual statements above are grounded in my CV, transcript, employment history, and goals note. No formal disciplinary finding has been reported.
